newsitem.title: USA: U S West Media selling cable systems in 3 states.
newsitem.headline: U S West Media selling cable systems in 3 states.

text.p: U S West Media Group said Tuesday it reached definitive agreements to sell cable systems in three states in two separate transactions.

In one agreement, U S West Media said, it will sell its Minneapolis-St. Paul systems for $600 million to Charter Communications Inc and two partners, Kelso & Co and an unidentified affiliate of E.M. Warburg, Pincus & Co LLC. All three buyers are privately held.
A separate agreement involves the sale of Media Group's systems in Twin Falls, Idaho, and Ellensburg, Wash., to Tele-Communications Inc for an undisclosed sum, the company said in a statement.
"We have chosen not to disclose those terms," Rob Stoddard, a spokesman for U S West Media told Reuters in response to an inquiry.

The sale price for the Minnesota systems represents 10 times their projected 1997 cash flow, U S West Media said. The systems serve 290,000 subscribers, about 60 percent of cable subscribers in the nation's 14th largest television market.

U S West Media said the Minnesota and Idaho systems are being sold to comply with U.S. Federal Communications Commission requirements governing the November 1996 merger of Continental Cablevision Inc., which now operates as MediaOne.

U S West Media said it had faced an August 15 deadline to shed its Minnesota and Idaho properties because they overlap with the phone operations of U S West Communications Group . U S West Media and U S West Communications are publicly traded subsidiaries of U S West Inc, a privately owned holding company.
Federal law prohibits a company from owning both cable and phone operations in the same geographic region.

The sale of the Ellensburg, Wash., system was not required by the FCC because U S West Communications does not serve that part of Washington, although it serves other parts of the state, U S West Media said.
